answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can charge every new identity a refundable stake that is only returned after a history of useful, attested work, like a falcon that must prove its hunting skill before joining the flock. A fable of effortless entry is the attacker dream: free accounts cost nothing to spawn, so the network echoes with sock puppets. With stake plus a slow reputation ramp, each fake identity costs real capital and weeks of waiting, so flooding the market becomes more expensive than any reward it could steal.
